questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'. Satya is always great to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'.
Satya is always  great to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The word "great" is incorrect in this context.
  • The correct word should be "grateful," which means showing appreciation.
  • Thus, the sentence should use "grateful" to convey the correct meaning.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: Satya is always grateful to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "greatful" – This is a misspelling of the correct word "grateful."
  • Option 2: "thanked" – This word is incorrect as it does not fit the context of the sentence.
  • Option 3: "no substitution" – This would be incorrect as the original sentence contains an error that needs to be corrected.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Epitome
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Epitome
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Expansion.

Key Points

  • The word "epitome" means a perfect example of a particular quality or type. (सर्वोत्कृष्ट उदाहरण)
    • Example: She is the epitome of elegance and grace.
  • "Expansion" refers to the action of becoming larger or more extensive. (विस्तार)
    • Example: The rapid expansion of the company led to increased job opportunities.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'epitome' is 'expansion'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.
Note: Expansion has been marked as the correct answer in the official answer key.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Exhort (प्रोत्साहित करना): Strongly encourage or urge someone to do something.
    • Example: The coach exhorted the team to give their best performance.
  • Lucid (स्पष्ट): Expressed clearly; easy to understand.
    • Example: His explanation of the complex theory was remarkably lucid.
  • Precise (सटीक): Marked by exactness and accuracy of expression or detail.
    • Example: The instructions need to be precise so that there is no confusion.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of "have" instead of "has" to match the singular subject "Mr. Surya."
  • The correct verb form for the singular subject should be "has".
  • The correct phrase should be "has no interior," ensuring grammatical correctness and subject-verb agreement.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 4 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "Mr. Surya has no interior motive in offering you support."
 
Additional Information
  • 1: "Mr. Surya" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • 3: "you support." – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • 2: "motive in offering" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The team always anticipate a bowling friendly pitch on their easy victory in the T20 matches.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The team always anticipate a bowling friendly pitch on their easy victory in the T20 matches.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The preposition "for" is the most appropriate to indicate purpose or intended outcome.
  • The sentence suggests that the team anticipates a bowling-friendly pitch as beneficial for their easy victory, making "pitch for their easy victory" the correct substitution.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: The team always anticipate a bowling-friendly pitch for their easy victory in the T20 matches.
 
Additional Information
  • pitch over: Incorrect because "over" does not fit the context of purpose or expectation.
  • pitch to: Incorrect because "to" suggests direction rather than purpose.
  • pitch of: Incorrect because "of" implies possession or a feature, which is not suitable here.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The team will announce the winner tomorrow.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The team will announce the winner tomorrow.

options.text: The team will announce tomorrow the winner.
options.html: The team will announce tomorrow the winner.

options.text: The winner will announce tomorrow by the team.
options.html: The winner will announce tomorrow by the team.

options.text: The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow.
options.html: The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow.

options.text: Tomorrow will be announced the winner by the team.
options.html: Tomorrow will be announced the winner by the team.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "The team will announce the winner tomorrow."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the winner" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "will announce" to "will be announced" (future simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the team."
  • Ensure the time phrase "tomorrow" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "The team will announce tomorrow the winner." – This is not in passive voice.
  • Option 2: "The winner will announce tomorrow by the team." – Incorrect structure.
  • Option 4: "Tomorrow will be announced the winner by the team." – Incorrect structure.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor of a sea-side apartment, as she is fearful of heights. She is suffering from ________.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor of a sea-side apartment, as she is fearful of heights. She is suffering from ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'acrophobia'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "acrophobia" means an extreme or irrational fear of heights.
  • Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor because she is fearful of heights.

​Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.

Complete Sentence: Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor of a sea-side apartment, as she is fearful of heights. She is suffering from acrophobia.

Additional Information
  • Heliophobia: means an extreme or irrational fear of sunlight.
  • Claustrophobia: means an extreme or irrational fear of confined places.
  • Sociophobia: means an extreme or irrational fear of social situations or interactions.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The homophone for the word 'there' is _______.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The homophone for the word 'there' is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option (2)' i.e. 'their'.
Key Points
  • There: Refers to a place (वहां)
    • Example: We will meet there at 5 PM.
  • Their: A possessive pronoun (उनका)
    • Example: Their car is parked outside.
  • They’re: A contraction of 'they are' (वे हैं)
    • Example: They’re going to the park.
Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Option 2'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Turned a deaf ear to
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Turned a deaf ear to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Disregarded.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Turned a deaf ear to" means to ignore or refuse to listen to someone or something. (अनसुना करना)
    • Example: Despite numerous complaints, the manager turned a deaf ear to the employees' concerns.
  • "Disregarded" means to pay no attention to; ignore. (अवहेलना करना)
    • Example: He disregarded the warnings and went ahead with his plan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Disregarded.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • At intervals (समय-समय पर): Occurring at certain periods of time.
    • Example: The bells rang at intervals throughout the day.
  • By any means (किसी भी तरह से): In any way possible.
    • Example: We need to finish this project by any means necessary.
  • Rebuked (फटकारा): Express sharp disapproval or criticism of someone because of their behavior or actions.
    • Example: The teacher rebuked the student for his rudeness.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. An elephant is a large mammal.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
An elephant is a  large  mammal.

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tiny.

    • Example: The kitten was so tiny that it could fit in the palm of my hand.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Bumper (विशाल): Exceptionally large or abundant.

    • Example: The firefighter's heroic actions saved many lives during the blaze.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bracket to fill in the blank. The modern work is deliberately _______ (ambiguous).
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bracket to fill in the blank.
The modern work is deliberately _______ (ambiguous).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. certain.

Key Points

  • The word "ambiguous" means something that is unclear or open to more than one interpretation. (अस्पष्ट)
    • Example: The instructions he gave were so ambiguous that no one knew what to do.
  • "Certain" refers to something that is definite, clear, and not open to doubt. (निश्चित)
    • Example: She is certain about her decision to pursue a career in medicine.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'ambiguous' is 'certain'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. certain.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Puzzling (परेशान करने वाला): Something that is confusing or difficult to understand.
    • Example: The disappearance of the keys was puzzling to everyone in the house.
  • Dubious (संदेहजनक): Something that is doubtful or not to be relied upon.
    • Example: He made some dubious claims about his past achievements.
  • Vague (अनिश्चित): Not clear or specific.
    • Example: Her directions were so vague that we got lost on the way.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. Smoking in B. Your youth stunts C. The body and D. Clouds the brain
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. Smoking in
B. Your youth stunts
C. The body and
D. Clouds the brain
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (1) i.e. ABCD
Key Points
  • The sentence begins with the subject "Smoking in," which is correctly indicated by part (A). 
  • Following the subject, "your youth stunts" (AB) continues the logical sequence, making it clear what the subject is affecting.
  • The next part, "the body and," starts the explanation about the effects of smoking, indicated by (C).
  • Ending with "clouds the brain" (D) completes the sentence by stating the final effect.
Therefore, the correct answer is ABCD.
Additional Information
  • Option 2 (CABD): This option starts with "the body and your youth stunts clouds the brain," which is grammatically incorrect and does not make sense.
  • Option 3 (DCBA): This option starts with "clouds the brain the body and your youth stunts smoking in," which is a jumbled and incoherent sentence.
  • Option 4 (DBCA): This option starts with "clouds the brain smoking in the body and your youth stunts," which is also a jumbled and incoherent sentence structure.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Barbarity
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Barbarity
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Compassion.

Key Points

  • The word "barbarity" means extreme cruelty or brutality. (क्रूरता)
    • Example: The barbarity of the attack shocked everyone.
  • "Compassion" refers to sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others. (दया)
    • Example: She was filled with compassion for the homeless children.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'barbarity' is 'compassion'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Compassion.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Callous (निर्दयी): Showing or having an insensitive and cruel disregard for others.
    • Example: His callous comments about the accident were upsetting.
  • Compromise (समझौता): An agreement or settlement of a dispute that is reached by each side making concessions.
    • Example: They finally reached a compromise after hours of negotiation.
  • Rivalry (प्रतिद्वंद्विता): Competition for the same objective or for superiority in the same field.
    • Example: There is a fierce rivalry between the two football teams.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold. His mother never held a grudge against his father.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold.
His mother never held a grudge against his father.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. benevolence.

Key Points

  • The word "grudge" means a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury. (द्वेष)
    • Example: She held a grudge against her colleague for getting the promotion she wanted.
  • "Benevolence" refers to the quality of being well-meaning and kindly. (भलाई)
    • Example: Her benevolence was evident when she donated generously to the charity.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'grudge' is 'benevolence'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. benevolence.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Rancour (कड़वाहट): Bitterness or resentfulness, especially when long-standing.
    • Example: The rancour between the two families had lasted for generations.
  • Revulsion (घृणा): A sense of disgust and loathing.
    • Example: She felt a sense of revulsion at the cruelty of the act.
  • Malevolence (दुर्भावना): The state or condition of being malevolent; having or showing a wish to do evil to others.
    • Example: His eyes were full of malevolence as he plotted his revenge.

questions.question: In the following sentence, four words have been underlined, out of which one word is MISSPELT. Select the option with the MISSPELT word. In spite of the dilemma that preveiled during the discussion sessions, the committee remained committed to finding an amicable solution to the issue.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following sentence, four words have been underlined, out of which one word is MISSPELT. Select the option with the MISSPELT word.

In spite of the dilemma that preveiled during the discussion sessions, the committee remained committed to finding an amicable solution to the issue.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

The misspelled word is 'preveiled'.

  • The correct spelling would be 'prevailed'.
  • The word 'prevailed' is a verb which means 'to be widespread or current; to exist generally'. (प्रचलित होना)
    • For Example : Despite the challenges, order finally prevailed in the meeting. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer would be 'preveiled'.

 

Additional Information

Let's understand the meanings of the other marked words - 

  • Amicable - having a spirit of friendliness; without serious disagreement or rancor (मैत्रीपूर्ण)
  • Committee - a group of people appointed for a specific function by a larger group (समिति)
  • Dilemma - a situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially ones that are equally undesirable (दुविधा)

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Don’t let Dylan fool you!
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Don’t let Dylan fool you!

options.text: Do not be fooled by Dylan.
options.html: Do not be fooled by Dylan.

options.text: Do not ever be fooled by Dylan.
options.html: Do not ever be fooled by Dylan.

options.text: Do not be fool by Dylan.
options.html: Do not be fool by Dylan.

options.text: Do not have been fooled by Dylan.
options.html: Do not have been fooled by Dylan.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "Don’t let Dylan fool you!"
  • To convert to passive voice: Start with "Do not be fooled."
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Dylan."
  • Ensure the command form is retained in the passive voice structure.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "Do not be fooled by Dylan."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "Do not ever be fooled by Dylan." – Though grammatically correct, it unnecessarily adds emphasis that is not in the original sentence.
  • Option 3: "Do not be fool by Dylan." – Incorrect verb form; "fool" should be "fooled."
  • Option 4: "Do not have been fooled by Dylan." – Incorrect construction for a command sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.

  • The blank requires a word that appropriately describes the three states of sleeping, dreaming, and waking.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The blank is describing individuals who have gained a profound understanding of transcendental knowledge.
  • The word "deep" is most appropriate in this context, as it emphasizes the intensity and depth of their knowledge.
  • Using "deep" conveys that their knowledge is comprehensive and insightful, aligning with the philosophical tone of the passage.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The word "says" is the most suitable option to fill the blank because it denotes a present assertion or universal truth attributed to Adi Shankaracharya.
  • The use of "says" keeps the statement in the present context, which aligns with the timeless nature of the teachings being referenced.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "‘The world and life is a myth and it keeps on changing,’ says Adi Shankaracharya, the greatest ‘Advaita’ preacher."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "tells by" – This phrase is grammatically incorrect and does not fit in the sentence structure.
  • Option 2: "was said" – This implies a past action, which is inconsistent with the ongoing relevance of the teaching.
  • Option 3: "saying" – This participle form cannot function as the main verb in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The blank refers to the idea expressed by Adi Shankaracharya, stating that the world and life are myths that change. The correct word should reflect the nature of the world he describes.
  • The term "unreal" appropriately captures the concept of an illusory or mythical world as described in the passage.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "‘What he said is that it is from one unreal world to another unreal world."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "confused" – This does not align with the abstract and philosophical nature of the passage.
  • Option 2: "reality" – While it fits grammatically, it contradicts the description of the world as mythical and changing.
  • Option 4: "unimaginary" – This is not a standard English word and does not fit the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • In this context, "is gained" is the most suitable option because it suggests that the happiness is achieved or obtained during sleep, which aligns with the idea that real happiness is found when the mind is absent.
  • "Gained" is in the passive voice and reflects an ongoing state rather than an active process. The phrase "the real happiness is gained" suggests that it is a state attained during sleep, where the mind is absent and the physical world is not present.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "During sleep, as the mind is absent and so is the physical world, the real happiness is gained."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "gains" – This would imply that happiness is actively obtained by something or someone, which is not the intended meaning in this passive context.
  • Option 3: "gained" – This is a past tense form, which does not fit with the general and ongoing nature of the sentence.
  • Option 4: "was gained" – This would suggest a completed action, but the passage discusses an ongoing state, making "is gained" the correct choice.
